chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a man who buys from another man the wool of one hundred ewes and what is in their bellies of pregnancy for such and such dirhams?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that; if there is not pregnancy in their bellies, the capital of his wealth is in the wool.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying sheep and their unborn lambs for a fixed price?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the sale of wool with unborn lambs, establishing that the primary capital value rests with the wool, thereby mitigating uncertainty (gharar) regarding the offspring. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of attributing value to the dominant asset when the secondary component is contingent, a nuance often discussed in the context of bay' al-gharar. It underscores the practical flexibility in commercial transactions provided the core commodity is clearly defined and valued.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a man who buys the wool of one hundred sheep and whatever is in their bellies from the pregnancies with such and such Dirhams?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that if there does not happen to be pregnancies in their bellies, the capital of his wealth would be in regarding the wool’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub Ibrahim al-Karkhiy who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who buys wool of a hundred sheep from another man and what is in their womb for so amount of dirham. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful; in case there is nothing in their womb he has his capital in the wool.’”
